obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1: Hotels
citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
basis: Acquirer A requires an annual QSA Report on Compliance. The division designs, connects and operates the PMS, POS, payment and property networks of the 58 managed hotels whose owners are the merchants of record, so it also validates as a service provider

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1: Attractions
citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
basis: Acquirer B requires a QSA Report on Compliance for about 41 million card transactions a year

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1: Vacation Ownership
citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
basis: Acquirer C requires an annual SAQ D for Merchants; sales gallery terminals connect to division workstations

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1: corporate shared services (SYS-G4)
citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
basis: SYS-G4 tokenization, vault, gateway integration and hosted payment form serve all three divisions and are in each validation; the 2026 service provider ROC covers them in full

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Hotels and group
basis: For-profit companies. The division operates the systems of 58 managed hotels (FTC v. Wyndham Worldwide Corp., 799 F.3d 236 (3d Cir. 2015)); group privacy notices and SYS-G5

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Attractions
basis: For-profit operator of the park app, precise location and finger-scan gate data

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Vacation Ownership
basis: For-profit companies; the finance subsidiary is not a bank or another entity carved out by 45(a)(2)

obligation: FTC/FACTA Disposal Rule: all divisions
basis: Background reports are used for hiring in every division, and the finance subsidiary holds consumer reports in loan files

obligation: State breach notification laws: all divisions and group
basis: Guests, visitors and owners live in every state; the law of each state where affected individuals reside applies. Hotels is also a third-party agent to managed hotel owners

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification and data security): all divisions
basis: Headquarters, 26 Florida hotels, the Florida destination resort parks and Florida timeshare plans; Florida personal information includes biometric data and geolocation (worked example for state law)

obligation: Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act: all divisions
basis: No Illinois operations; finger-scan gates run only at the 3 Florida parks. The statute text was not verified (N72-R05 is marked unverified)

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed): all divisions and group
basis: Final rule not published; the group exceeds the SBA size standard, so the proposed size-based criterion would cover it

obligation: Nevada Gaming Commission Regulation 5.260: all divisions
basis: No gaming licensee in the group; no casino or gaming at any park or resort

obligation: NIGC MICS information technology: all divisions
basis: No tribal gaming operation

obligation: BSA/AML program for casinos: all divisions
basis: Not a casino or card club

obligation: COPPA Rule: Attractions (Junior Explorers kids' club)
basis: The kids' club in the park app is an online service directed to children, and Cris Santos Parks and Attractions, LLC operates it

obligation: COPPA Rule: Hotels, Vacation Ownership and group
basis: The kids' club is the only service in the group directed to children

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Vacation Ownership finance subsidiary
basis: A finance company (314.1(b)) that extends consumer credit for timeshare purchases (about 126,000 active loans) and is not a bank; the 314.6 exceptions for fewer than 5,000 consumers do not apply

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: corporate shared services
citation: 16 CFR 314.2 (customer information handled by or on behalf of affiliates)
applies: Yes (for the finance subsidiary's customer information)
basis: Bank account and routing numbers for about 212,000 autopay owners, about 151,000 of them loan customers, were copied to SYS-G5 in 2025; the group SOC monitors the division

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Hotels and Attractions
basis: Neither division extends credit or is otherwise a financial institution

obligation: FTC Red Flags Rule: finance subsidiary
basis: Consumer timeshare loans are covered accounts; the board approved the Identity Theft Prevention Program in 2019

obligation: ECOA and Regulation B: finance subsidiary
basis: Credit decisions on timeshare loans, including those of the AI credit model

obligation: FCRA adverse action duties: finance subsidiary
basis: The credit model uses consumer reports; P10 lists the adverse action duties for counsel to confirm. Not analyzed in P03

obligation: FTC rule on unfair or deceptive fees: Hotels, Attractions, Vacation Ownership
basis: Short-term lodging at 88 hotels, 24 of them with a mandatory fee; vacation rentals sold through the CRS; separately ticketed park events. Whether general admission park tickets are live-event tickets is a watch item

obligation: Florida guest register: Hotels
basis: The PMS is the guest register for the 26 Florida hotels

obligation: Florida price gouging during declared emergencies: Hotels
basis: The statute names dwelling units and commodities; a counsel memo treats room rates as covered

obligation: Florida timeshare managing entity records: Vacation Ownership
basis: The division manages Florida timeshare plans and reserves unused owner inventory for rental (AI-007)

obligation: Florida Digital Bill of Rights: all divisions
basis: Revenue exceeds $1 billion, but the group earns less than 50% of revenue from online advertising and runs no consumer smart speaker and voice command service and no app store with 250,000 or more applications

obligation: CCPA and CPPA regulations (cybersecurity audit): all divisions and group
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.; Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7120-7124
applies: Yes (loan data subject to GLBA is excluded from consumer rights)
basis: 5 California hotels; revenue far above $26,625,000; personal information of more than 250,000 California consumers. First audit report due 2028-04-01

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure: group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; divisions contribute incident facts through the group

obligation: HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules: all divisions
basis: Park first-aid stations do not bill health plans electronically, so no division is a covered entity

obligation: Bank and credit union safeguards rules: finance subsidiary
citation: 12 CFR Part 30 App. B; 12 CFR Part 748
basis: No entity holds a bank or credit union charter; the finance subsidiary is subject to the FTC GLBA rules instead

obligation: Federal contract safeguarding clauses: all divisions
basis: The group has no federal contracts

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 (AI in consequential decisions): finance subsidiary and Attractions hiring
basis: Not in effect during this assessment; would reach credit decisions about Colorado consumers from 2027-01-01, and the proposed screening tool only if used for Colorado hiring

obligation: Title VII and ADA for AI hiring tools: Attractions (proposed AI-005)
basis: The proposed seasonal applicant screening tool would rank applicants; employment law duties apply to any tool used in hiring. The tool is not approved

obligation: Merchant agreements with Acquirers A, B and C
basis: Validation method per division and acquirer notice within 24 hours of a suspected compromise

obligation: Management agreements with owners of the 58 managed hotels
basis: Agreements signed since 2020 set security responsibilities, the PCI DSS acknowledgment and owner notice within 24 hours; the 31 signed before 2020 do not

obligation: Association management agreements: Vacation Ownership
basis: The division manages billing, records and reservations for 24 owners' associations under management agreements

obligation: SOC 2 requests from managed hotel owners, lenders and associations
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; owner requests
applies: Yes (requested for Hotels SL-1 and Vacation Ownership SL-2; Attractions out of scope)
basis: Owners and their lenders asked for SOC 2 in 2026; the 24 associations rely on the division's billing and records
